figures.caption: **What to see: each declared significance test is drawn with both its uncorrected and its multiplicity-corrected interval side by side, so a reader can see directly which results survive correction for testing many hypotheses at once and which do not.** The multiplicity family at a glance. Top: the primary paired effects, each drawn as the favored share of its discordant pairs with nested whiskers: the exact *marginal* Clopper–Pearson {{SHARE_CONFIDENCE_PCT}}% interval, and behind it the family-corrected interval at one minus the Bonferroni per-test level, whose exclusion of one half is the verdict the badge states ([@tbl:multiplicity_family] is the exact-value record). These are share intervals, not treatment-effect intervals: the axis is the conditional win share among discordant pairs, its null is one half rather than zero, and converting a row to the accuracy scale requires the discordance rate through [@eq:paired_difference]. Two reference lines are drawn: the McNemar null at the structural constant 1/2 (dashed) and the fixed power reference share {{STAT_REFERENCE_SHARE}} (dotted). A statistics column beside the forest gives, per row, the discordant $n$ and the evaluated population it is drawn from with its unit; whether a cluster-robust re-analysis covers that same population, and if so its clustering unit, cluster count and level, or else that the drawn interval is not cluster-adjusted; the exact power at the reference share (matching the table); the corrected-level badge; the Holm verdict; and which held-back population the confirmatory protocol registers to re-score the row, with whether that run has happened. Every verdict word is read directly from a recorded boolean rather than inferred from the geometry beside it, and the panel footer states how many of the family survive each correction. Power at the observed share is a monotone transform of the p-value and is not drawn. Bottom: the Stage 6 sign test's one- and two-sided p values, drawn against the familywise {{STAT_FAMILYWISE_ALPHA}}, the fixed Bonferroni per-test {{STAT_BONFERRONI_ALPHA}}, this member's Holm step-down threshold {{STAT_HOLM_STAGE6_THRESHOLD}}, and the relaxed threshold for the collapsed family, derived in code as the familywise level over the size that {{STAT_FAMILY_SIZE}} members become when the subsample re-analyses are counted once. The shaded band runs from the fixed threshold to the Holm one: that is the interval in which the verdict depends on which of two equally valid familywise corrections is applied. Where the two-sided test lands relative to that band is what the recorded booleans state: the fixed-threshold flag is {{STAT_STAGE6_FAMILYWISE_CONFIRMED}} and the Holm verdict is {{STAT_HOLM_STAGE6_REJECTED}}. Of the two disclosed relaxations only the one-sided test crosses; the family-size relaxation does not rescue the result, and it is drawn to show that it does not. The figure refuses to draw if the corrected Clopper–Pearson verdict recomputed from the recorded raw discordant counts contradicts any recorded exclusion boolean; if a drawn marginal whisker straddles 1/2 while its corrected verdict claims exclusion; if the drawn Holm geometry contradicts the recorded Holm verdict; if Holm's threshold is drawn below Bonferroni's; or if the drawn p-threshold geometry contradicts the recorded survival flag or either disclosed fragility direction. It also refuses to draw if a recorded corrected interval disagrees with the recorded survivor set it is the dual of, if the Bonferroni survivors are not a subset of Holm's, if a survivor list disagrees with its recorded count or names a label outside the declared family, if a discordant count exceeds the population it is drawn from, or if the protocol maps a different number of members to a completed confirmatory population than the ledger counts as scored.
figures.label: fig:multiplicity_forest

figures.caption: **What to see: no arm in this project is reported as "no effect" — every null and near-null is drawn instead as a bounded interval, so a reader can tell a tight bound from an inconclusive one at a glance.** Every null and near-null in the project, drawn as a bounded effect. Top: the arms measured on an accuracy difference, each with its exact conditional {{BOUND_CONFIDENCE_PCT}}% paired interval, its discordant pair count over the population that produced it with that population's unit, and whether a cluster-robust re-analysis covers the same arm or none was recorded; the dashed line is no difference, and the established lexical high-weight contrast is drawn there for scale as the Stage 2 contrast is in the middle panel. Middle: the directional-share arms, with the familywise-established Stage 2 G2P contrast drawn beside the Stage 6 near-null as the live positive control. Bottom: the same arms against the pairs each produced, on a log axis, with the shaded region marking arms that cannot support an equivalence claim at any outcome because they never produced enough discordant pairs — the point being that a bounded null and an unresolvable one look identical in a table and different here. Every value is derived at render time from recorded counts by the function that produced the recorded external-benchmark bounds. The nested-token punctuation-oracle intervention is excluded because its valid interval resamples whole documents. A drawn interval that disagrees with its recorded endpoints, an arm placed inside the shaded region while its interval is narrow enough to exclude the declared smallest interesting effect, an established contrast drawn as though it were a null, or a cluster count that does not partition the population it claims to cover would each falsify this panel. A bound stated over an unnamed unit cannot be judged wide or narrow, which is why each row names its own.

figures.caption: Level 2's learned emission and transition, computed at generation time through the same `build_g2p_emission` and `build_phone_transition` calls the shipped agent uses. Left: the letter-to-phone emission $\mathbf{A}$, {{STAGE0_LETTER_ALPHABET_SIZE}} letter observations over {{PHONEME_COUNT_39}} phones, counted over letters and phones that share an index in a length-matched word. Its bright ridge is that co-occurrence and is read as nothing more: where a phone's conventional spelling is one letter the ridge cell also happens to be a grapheme-phoneme correspondence, and where the phone is spelled by a digraph, or the pairing hands its letter to a neighboring phone, the ridge cell is an artifact of the pairing rule. The panel is therefore not evidence of a learned phonographic relationship. Right: the phone-bigram transition $\mathbf{B}$ on the same log color scale. The panels' different shapes are the point: an emission and a transition here cannot be confused by slot alone, which is exactly the mis-wiring class Part A could not detect structurally. A rebuilt emission whose columns were near-uniform — each phone's letter mass spread flat across the alphabet, so that the co-index statistic carried no information at all — would falsify the caption's reading of the left panel, and the peak cells printed beneath the panels are re-derived from the matrices on every build, so the figure refuses to draw numbers the model does not contain.

figures.caption: The word level across lexicon size, on nested frequency-ranked prefixes of the Brown lexicon. Left: coverage of the held-out stream, measured against the original held-out token count at every rung so the percentages share one denominator. The final rung contains every training type that meets the word-length eligibility rule. Right: per-emission perplexity for the level and for the letter-bigram comparator, on log axes. The dashed line is where the dense `pymdp` transition stops fitting in memory; the closed form is exact beyond it, which is the distinction between what can be *run* and what can be *measured*. The comparator is estimated once on the full training frequencies and re-scored per rung, not re-fit, so its curve moves only with the evaluation population. The panel is falsified if the shared-denominator gain fails to rise monotonically, if any rung's recomputed gain disagrees with its recorded pair, or if numeric coverage and perplexity fail to rise together. Curve-crossing is deliberately *not* offered as a falsifier: on nested frequency-ranked prefixes of a Zipfian corpus these curves cannot cross, so a reader should treat their separation as arithmetic rather than as evidence.
